candidates.title: VoteWeighting.removeNominee zeroes a nominee's bias but never clears its slope from pointsSum/changesSum, so _getSum keeps decaying the global weight sum by a phantom slope
candidates.description: removeNominee() sets pointsWeight[nomineeHash][nextTime].bias=0 and pointsSum[nextTime].bias = oldSum-oldWeight, but does NOT decrement the removed nominee's slope contribution from pointsSum[nextTime].slope, nor remove its scheduled changesSum[...] entries. Slope cleanup is deferred to the per-user revokeRemovedNomineeVotingPower(). Until (and unless) every voter for that nominee individually revokes, _getSum() continues to subtract the removed nominee's slope*WEEK from the global sum each week, so the total weight sum decays faster than it should. Because nomineeRelativeWeight = nomineeWeight / totalSum drives Dispenser reward allocation, an over-decayed totalSum inflates remaining nominees' relative weights (mis-allocating emissions), and can clamp the sum bias to 0 prematurely.

candidates.title: VoteWeighting._maxAndSub clamps bias/slope subtractions to 0, silently losing weight on vote updates (deviation from Curve's checked subtraction)
candidates.description: voteForNomineeWeights updates pointsWeight/pointsSum bias and slope via _maxAndSub(a,b)=a>b?a-b:0. Where Curve's GaugeController uses checked subtraction (reverting on inconsistency), Olas clamps to 0. If the accumulated old bias/slope exceeds the freshly-checkpointed value + new delta (e.g. due to ordering of _getWeight/_getSum checkpoints vs the user's stale oldSlope.end), the clamp hides an underflow and permanently drops weight from the sum/nominee, drifting the accounting. Needs an end-to-end multi-voter sequence to bound exploitability vs. mere precision loss.

candidates.title: VoteWeighting.removeNominee emits OwnerOnly(owner, msg.sender) with swapped argument order (QA)
candidates.description: The error is declared OwnerOnly(address sender, address owner) but removeNominee reverts with OwnerOnly(owner, msg.sender) — arguments swapped vs every other call site. The access check itself (msg.sender != owner) is correct; only the revert data is misleading. QA/informational.

candidates.title: StakingBase Proportional reward distribution sends to mapAgentInstanceOperators(); a zero/reverting operator address bricks claim() and non-enforced unstake()
candidates.description: In _getRewardReceiversAndAmounts (RewardDistributionType.Proportional, the new v12 path), receivers[i] = IService.mapAgentInstanceOperators(agentInstances[i]) and _withdraw loops _transfer to each. If any agent instance maps to address(0) (or, for ERC20 staking, an operator that reverts/blacklists), the whole _withdraw reverts, bricking _claim and the non-enforced _unstake reward path for that service. forcedUnstake (enforced) still works but forfeits the reward to availableRewards, so funds are not permanently lost but the earned reward is unclaimable. Bounded by whether a deployed service can have a zero/hostile operator.

candidates.title: ServiceManager.registerAgentsWithSignature does not validate msg.value in the token-secured path, stranding excess ETH (QA)
candidates.description: The non-signature registerAgents() checks msg.value == agentInstances.length*BOND_WRAPPER for token-secured services, but registerAgentsWithSignature() omits that check and forwards exactly agentInstances.length*BOND_WRAPPER to the registry regardless of msg.value. Any excess ETH sent by the service owner remains stuck in ServiceManager. QA/best-practice — caller error, no theft.
